subject: BrightLeaf DPA: forwarding/limited-use carveouts + onshore fallback and subprocessor EdgeCacheX
messages:
From: Ben Walters <ben.walters@brightleafhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@brightleafhealth.com>
Date: 2027-01-09T15:12:00Z
Subject: BrightLeaf DPA - quick questions on forwarding exception and new CDN vendor

Thanks for the redline, team. A couple quick items the legal ops folks flagged while we review: 

1) Forwarding / limited-use carveout — our privacy counsel wants to ensure there's a narrow permitted-forwarding exception for: (a) routing telemetry for fraud detection to our fraud provider, and (b) one-off support escalations to our security vendor. They want to avoid a broad "limited use" definition that allows onward commercial use. Can you confirm how Redwood intends to carve that?

2) Subprocessor: we saw EdgeCacheX listed as a caching/CDN subprocessor in the addendum. They operate in multiple US regions and have a failover site in Puerto Rico. We need to understand data residency, encryption-at-rest, and whether an "onshore fallback" is available in a declared US state if there is an outage.

Attaching our current redline for reference. Happy to hop on a short call — available tomorrow morning ET.

-Ben
Senior Product Manager
BrightLeaf Health

Subject: Re: BrightLeaf DPA - quick questions on forwarding exception and new CDN vendor

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear asks. High level responses below; Marissa can comment on precise contract language.

1) Forwarding / limited-use: Redwood's approach is to keep the service-provider (CCPA/CPRA) model strict: no commercial resale or derivative commercial use. We can support a narrowly worded exception for telemetry routing to third-party security/fraud tooling and for support escalation when needed for incident response. We'll propose language limited to "routing necessary for security, fraud prevention, or explicit support requests initiated by Customer" with strict prohibition on non-security commercialization. Marissa: I suggest we propose the following sentence to BrightLeaf: \"Provider may disclose Customer Personal Information to Subprocessors solely to provide security, fraud detection, or support services on behalf of Customer; such disclosures are limited to data strictly necessary for those services and are prohibited from being used for Provider commercial purposes.\"

2) EdgeCacheX: operationally they are a short-term cache/CDN partner we use for edge delivery. They do operate across US regions and their default pattern is multi-region failover. We do offer an onshore fallback option for certain customers (Dedicated/Private) that pins caching to a region; for hosted plans this is an add-on. For BrightLeaf we can commit to a documented onshore fallback play: if EdgeCacheX cannot guarantee US-state residency during an incident, Redwood will failover to our onshore fallback pool (explicitly listable regions) within the SLO. We'll capture the SLO and remediation steps in the addendum.

I'll propose language and an incident playbook snippet — Marissa, can you weigh in on the legal carve and retention limits?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jan 9, 2027 at 4:05 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Forwarding / limited-use: Redwood's approach is to keep the service-provider (CCPA/CPRA) model strict...
> 2) EdgeCacheX: operationally they are a short-term cache/CDN partner we use for edge delivery...

Ben / Legal Ops — looping in a short redline suggestion below. This preserves the SP/processor boundary and addresses the "narrow exception" request: 

Proposed clause (suggested insertion into US Privacy Addendum):
"Provider may transmit Customer Personal Information to third-party security, fraud-detection, or support subprocessors solely to perform services on behalf of Customer. Such transmissions shall be limited to the minimum data necessary, documented in the Subprocessor profile, and strictly prohibited from any secondary commercial use inconsistent with this Agreement. Provider shall maintain records of such transmissions and make them available to Customer upon reasonable request for audit purposes."

Retention/telemetry: For telemetry used for security/fraud, propose a maximum retention of 13 months unless Customer requests otherwise; production logs that contain PII will follow Customer deletion requests within 30 days of validated request (or earlier if the log is ephemeral).

EdgeCacheX specifics: we've reviewed the EdgeCacheX_subprocessor_profile.pdf. Key asks we will commit to in the addendum:
- Encryption at rest (AES-256) and TLS in transit.
- Ability to pin caching domain to a single listed US state/region on request as part of an "onshore fallback" play for BrightLeaf (operational cost applies).
- Audit evidence: EdgeCacheX can provide SOC2 Type II report and a recent encryption configuration snapshot; we will include both as attachments or references.

Ben: if Legal Ops still wants the forwarding exception to require prior written notice rather than a standing carve, we can accept notice for outbound sharing outside these narrowly defined categories.

I'll prepare the redline with the proposed retention and the EdgeCacheX clause for your review.

-Marissa
Head of Legal, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — that looks reasonable. A couple of follow-ups from our ops/security team: 

- Retention of telemetry at 13 months is acceptable if we can get a log-level deletion SLA (30 days) and a mechanism to request expungement with an audit token. Can you add a line that Redwood will provide a verifiable deletion token within 30 days after validated deletion requests for logs cached by EdgeCacheX?

- Onshore fallback: BrightLeaf would like the fallback to be bound to a named US "state" (e.g., Virginia or California) because our compliance program maps data residency to state-specific policies. Is Redwood able to name a default state (we prefer Virginia) or at least guarantee the fallback will be to a named state with notice?

If you can incorporate both items in the redline we'll share with our counsel. Also — can we have a short call tomorrow 10am ET to finalize?

-Ben
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: BrightLeaf DPA - quick questions on forwarding exception and new CDN vendor

Ben — quick operational answers ahead of the 10am ET call. 

1) Deletion token: we can provide a verifiable deletion token (UUID + signed timestamp) from EdgeCacheX for cached logs within 30 days of a validated deletion request. We'll include the schema for the token and a sample verification endpoint in the addendum (no PII returned from the endpoint; it only proves the deletion event and shard id).

2) Named onshore fallback state: for BrightLeaf we can commit to a primary onshore fallback region in Northern Virginia (us-east-1 equivalent). We'll document that the fallback pool will remain in the listed state unless pre-approved changes are requested by BrightLeaf. This will be captured as an operational SLA with a potential additional cost for region-pinning.

Karthik / Marissa: I'm attaching the operational playbook snippet (JIRA PRIV-742 will track the runbook) and will be on the call to walk through the token proof and failover timing.

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
